# AUTO-BLOCKING — reference for AI scene reconstruction (Blocking Studio)

> Injected into the multimodal LLM context for the "AI Auto-Blocking" call. Goal: from ONE
> reference image, output a ROUGH 3D blocking (primitives + a camera) the Blocking Studio
> can instantiate. This is a FIRST PASS to refine by hand over the reference overlay, not a
> metric reconstruction.

## Output contract — STRICT JSON only
Return ONLY a single JSON object, no prose, no markdown fences. Schema:
```
{
  "objects": [
    { "type": "<primitive>", "label": "<short name>",
      "position": [x, y, z], "rotation": [rx, ry, rz], "scale": [sx, sy, sz],
      "color": "#rrggbb",
      "image_anchor": [u, v] }
  ],
  "camera": { "focal_mm": <number>, "position": [x, y, z], "target": [x, y, z] },
  "notes": "<one short line, optional>"
}
```
- Coordinates: **Three.js convention** — **Y is up**, units are **meters**, the **ground is
  the plane y = 0**, objects rest ON the ground (their base at y≈0). Scene roughly centered
  near the origin.
- `rotation` in **degrees** (XYZ Euler). `scale` are multipliers (1 = default size).
- `color` = a hex sampled/estimated from the image for that object.
- `image_anchor` = the object's center in the image, NORMALIZED [u, v] with u,v in 0..1
  (u = left→right, v = top→bottom). The app samples a depth map at this point to refine the
  object's distance from camera, so give the most representative pixel of the object.

## Primitive types (map to Blocking Studio)
Use ONLY these `type` values: `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `cone`, `pyramid`, `plane`,
`dome`, `torus`, `car`, `bus`, `facade`, `human`, `null`.
- Pick the closest primitive for each salient object/volume in the image (a person ->
  `human`, a wall/building face -> `facade` or `box`, a vehicle -> `car`/`bus`, a ball ->
  `sphere`, a column -> `cylinder`, the floor is implicit, etc.).
- Keep it to the **main blocking volumes** (typically 2–8 objects), not every tiny detail.

## Orientation is MANDATORY (not just position)
Each object MUST be rotated to match its facing in the image — placement alone is not
enough. Read the object's heading from the image and set `rotation` (mainly **ry**, the yaw
around the vertical axis) so the primitive faces the same way.
- Primitives have an intrinsic FRONT: `car`/`bus` front = +Z, `human`/`facade` front = +Z
  (a human/facade faces +Z by default). Rotate `ry` so that front points where the real
  object points in the image (e.g. a car seen in 3/4 facing camera-left, a wall seen at an
  angle, a person looking right).
- Use perspective cues (which side/edge is visible, vanishing direction, which way a face/
  front is turned) to estimate yaw. Add `rx`/`rz` only if the object is clearly tilted.
- A car placed without the right yaw is WRONG even if its position is right — orientation
  must read correctly at a glance.

## Scale anchor
A standing **human ≈ 1.75 m tall**. Size everything relative to that. If the main subject is
a person, place it near the origin and scale the rest accordingly.

## Camera estimation
- `focal_mm`: estimate from perspective compression / field of view (wide ~16–24mm,
  natural ~50mm, portrait/telephoto ~85–135mm). Use the visible distortion and how much
  background is compressed.
- `position` + `target`: place the camera so its view roughly matches the reference framing
  (angle, height, shot size). `target` is the look-at point (usually the main subject's
  center). Eye-level ≈ camera y ~1.5m; low angle = lower y; high angle = higher y.
- Match the **shot size** (wide/medium/close) by camera distance to target.

## Monocular caveats (be reasonable, not exact)
- Depth from a single image is ambiguous: infer a PLAUSIBLE relative layout (left/right,
  near/far, on the ground), not exact distances.
- Order objects by apparent depth; keep them from overlapping unrealistically.
- Prefer a clean, minimal blocking the user can nudge — correctness of relative placement
  and camera framing matters more than precision.

## Example (shape only)
```
{"objects":[
  {"type":"human","label":"man","position":[0,0,0],"rotation":[0,15,0],"scale":[1,1,1],"color":"#caa37a"},
  {"type":"box","label":"desk","position":[0,0,0.8],"rotation":[0,0,0],"scale":[1.4,0.4,0.7],"color":"#5b4632"},
  {"type":"facade","label":"back wall","position":[0,0,-2.5],"rotation":[0,0,0],"scale":[5,3,0.2],"color":"#3a3f46"}
 ],
 "camera":{"focal_mm":35,"position":[1.2,1.5,3.2],"target":[0,1.1,0]},
 "notes":"eye-level 3/4 view, medium shot"}
```
